question: Which of the three candidate semantics for quota_caps?
answer: Reserved for lock-time. Working recommendation: (1) absolute usage ceiling with field rename to `percent_weekly_cap` and unbounded value. Reasons: (a) closest to current breaker code — minimal logic change. (b) field name then matches what it actually does. (c) operator mental model 'trip if weekly usage exceeds N%' is the most direct. Counter-argument for (3) per-volley delta ceiling: better answers 'how much will THIS plan cost'. Decide pre-impl with operator review.

question: Field rename vs. lift-the-bound-only?
answer: Reserved for lock-time. If semantic (1) wins, recommend renaming to `percent_weekly_cap` to make the unboundedness visible in the field name. If semantic (2) or (3) wins, the bound stays at 100 and the existing name `quota_caps` is fine. Either way, document the chosen name's contract in claude/shared/schemas/v1.0/<file>.json description so the next reader doesn't repeat the dogfood discovery.

question: Backfill strategy for existing Jarvis plans.
answer: Reserved for lock-time. Working plan: backfill in the same commit that subtree-pulls the new agent-conventions, so the repo is never in a state where the schema has bumped but plans haven't. List of plans needing edit: 2026-04-19-001, 2026-04-25-001, 2026-04-26-006, 2026-04-28-001, 2026-04-29-001, 2026-04-29-002, 2026-04-29-003, plus this plan itself. Verify with `python -m jarvis_orchestrate ... validate-all` (or equivalent) post-backfill.

question: Cross-project coordination — Glam, SpinDine.
answer: Reserved for lock-time. Neither Glam nor SpinDine declares orchestrator-level quota_caps in their plans (they consume agent-conventions only for the resolver + skill schemas). The version bump should still propagate via subtree pull but no plan edits required there. Confirm by grep of their docs/plans/ trees pre-impl.

question: Pause and re-scope this plan after vendor-native quota tracker plan lands?
answer: Yes. Status flips draft → blocked. Reason: operator review of the Anthropic Max dashboard on 2026-04-30 (showing 13% weekly while tracker showed 320%) surfaced that the underlying `percent_weekly` signal is wrong by ~25× (cache-token weighting + arbitrary 1B-token divisor + wrong window). The same shape of misalignment exists across all four vendors. The 'which of three semantics' framing of D001-D004 assumed `percent_weekly` was usable telemetry that just needed schema-bound alignment — that premise no longer holds. New plan `2026-04-30-001-fix-quota-tracker-vendor-native` replaces the tracker with per-vendor native windows + units + operator caps file, and rewrites F006 check_budget_ceiling to read the new state shape. Reactivation criterion: once that plan's F006 ships and the changelog dogfood re-runs green with the new state shape, this plan reactivates and reduces to (a) remove quota_caps field from plan.schema.json + plan_model.py, (b) update F006/F007 description text in parent plan 2026-04-19-001 to reflect per-vendor per-window model, (c) backfill any plan whose frontmatter still declares quota_caps so they validate after schema removal. D001-D004 above are not deleted — they remain as historical record of the semantic-pick framing that turned out to be the wrong question. Status enum has no 'paused' value; 'blocked' is the closest match and accurately describes the dependency.

question: Reactivation scope: should this plan also migrate cost-model + cost-guard skills off the legacy quota_state.json models{} mirror?
answer: Yes — scope expansion approved at F002 land time of 2026-04-30-001. Triggered by `rg 'percent_weekly|quota_state|models'` consumer scan during F002 design, which surfaced 5 active legacy-mirror consumers: orchestrator-side (circuit_breakers, supervisor._quota_gate, quota_admission, signoff_writer — all in 2026-04-30-001 F006's blast radius) and skill-side (claude/skills/cost-model/cost_model.py + claude/skills/cost-guard/cost_guard.py — outside that plan's scope, in plan 2026-04-28-001 #692 territory). 2026-04-30-001 F002 emits BOTH vendors{} v2 block AND legacy models{} mirror; F006 of that plan migrates orchestrator-side consumers but leaves the writer-side mirror in place because cost-model/cost-guard would silently break otherwise. This plan's reactivation now owns the final mirror removal: (a) update cost-model.py + cost-guard.py to read vendors{} primarily with fallback to models{} during their own cutover, (b) remove the writer-side legacy models{} block + LEGACY_MIRROR_NOTE constant from quota_check.py + the deprecated `percent_weekly: null` fields, (c) remove plan-level quota_caps field from plan.schema.json + plan_model.py (original D001-D004 territory), (d) update F006/F007 description text in parent plan 2026-04-19-001 to reflect per-vendor per-window model, (e) backfill any plan still declaring quota_caps so they validate. This is the linear-migration sequence: orchestrator-side first (in 2026-04-30-001 F006), then skills + writer-side mirror removal + schema cleanup (here in this plan's reactivation). Note: 2026-04-30-001 F002 _build_state codex legacy mirror uses rolling_7d for parity with the post-F001 weekly framing the cost-model/cost-guard skills assume; vendors{}.codex.windows.rolling_5h is what F006 reads for breaker decisions (Codex's actual subscriber-tier native window). When this plan migrates cost-model/cost-guard to vendors{}, those skills should re-tune their LLM budgets against the rolling_5h window for codex (since that's the meaningful subscriber-meter window) rather than continuing to project 7d totals.
